rules.land: every status, with its 100 m grade; the app hides what the land filter excludes
rules.text: Loose gravel beside water that you can park next to and dig: the analyzer's gravel bars and creek beds on a named river or creek, and gravel pits right beside one, within 150 m of a road a car can use, where at least one gravel-friendly stone's map is in its top 20%; every land status is listed with its grade. Ranked by the chance that a target stone is really in the gravel: reported finds within 3 km and finds upstream on the same river carry the weight, the stone map only nudges; then how well the river places the bar, its size and how close you can park. A few map picks per state (hot stone map, nothing reported) ride along as a test of the map. Not yet tested against trips.

spots.label: gravel bar
expect: Most of the gravel: speckled granite and hard quartzite and argillite (Belt rocks).

Far-travelled stones too, from the whole basin upstream: hard, well-rounded quartzite and other cobbles that do not match the local rock; agate, jasper and petrified wood ride a river this size a long way.
Garnet (map top 3%): dark red grains in the black sand at bar heads; a gold pan finds them.
Serpentine & jade (map top 2%): dark green, greasy-looking, very tough stones, often with a pale rind.
Quartz crystals (map top 16%): milky or clear quartz chunks, sometimes with flat crystal faces.
Staurolite & kyanite (map top 17%): brown crosses or blue blades in pebbles of schist.
Plus plenty of handsome banded or spotted river rock that is none of these; keep what you like.
